terms.meaning: a trail of links that shows the path from the top of a site to the current page
software that reads the page aloud for people who cannot see it
a hidden label that tells assistive software what an element means

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Trail of links and arrows
sections.what: Builds the navigation trail as a list, with each step a link. Arrows separate the steps, and the link can be drawn as another element if the page asks for that.
sections.why: Lets users move back up the site structure and tells screen readers that this block is navigation.
sections.watch_out: The separator setting is declared but not used, so a separator passed in as a setting does nothing.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Current page, arrow and three dots
sections.what: Shows the current page as plain text that cannot be clicked. Also provides the arrow between steps and a three-dot marker, with a hidden word More for screen readers, that stands in for hidden middle steps.
sections.why: Marks the current page so screen readers announce it as the current location. Reason not stated for labeling the current page as a link.
sections.watch_out: The three-dot part has a spelling error in its internal name, which does not change behavior but will show in debugging tools.

summary: A row of links showing where the user is in the site, such as Home then Products then the current page.
purpose: Lets users see their position in the site and jump back to higher levels.
why: Likely reason: a shared navigation trail. The labels that mark it as navigation are there so screen readers can identify it. Reason otherwise not stated.
how: Step 1: Builds the outer navigation box and its ordered list. Step 2: Builds each item and each link, where a link can be swapped for another element. Step 3: Builds the current page label, the arrow between items, and the three-dot marker for hidden steps. Step 4: Makes all the parts available to other files.
inputs: Links and text for each step, optional separators, and extra style classes or attributes.
outputs: A horizontal trail with links, arrows between steps, and a plain current-page label.
risks: The separator setting is declared but never used, so passing one has no effect and it is handed to the navigation box instead.
debug: If arrows are missing, check that the separator part is placed between items. If the trail is in the wrong order, check the item order passed in. If a link does not look like a link, check the link styles or the swapped element.
